messages.content:
The input lists customer reviews, each with a reference like "R1". Find themes
that reviewers raise: praise, complaints, or mixed reactions.

For each theme give:
- "theme": a short neutral label, for example "lid leaks".
- "polarity": positive, negative, mixed, or neutral.
- "review_refs": the references of every review that supports the theme. Use
  only references from the input. A review may support several themes.
- "terms": 1-4 short phrases a listing might use about this theme, for example
  "leak proof".
- "rationale": one sentence of at most 25 words that an auditor can check
  against the cited reviews.

Return at most 8 themes, the most frequently supported first. Do not invent
reviews, counts, or product features. Return an empty list if no theme is
supported.

<input>
{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "asin": "B0COMP0002",
      "rating": 5,
      "ref": "R1",
      "text": "Keeps ice for 24 hours, even in the car."
    },
    {
      "asin": "B0COMP0002",
      "rating": 4,
      "ref": "R2",
      "text": "Heavy but tough."
    },
    {
      "asin": "B0COMP0001",
      "rating": 5,
      "ref": "R3",
      "text": "Ice lasts all day."
    },
    {
      "asin": "B0COMP0001",
      "rating": 1,
      "ref": "R4",
      "text": "Lid leaks if it tips over."
    },
    {
      "asin": "B0COMP0001",
      "rating": 2,
      "ref": "R5",
      "text": "Straw lid leaked in my bag."
    },
    {
      "asin": "B0COMP0002",
      "rating": 2,
      "ref": "R6",
      "text": "Leaked all over my backpack."
    },
    {
      "asin": "B0COMP0003",
      "rating": 5,
      "ref": "R7",
      "text": "Kids love the straw."
    },
    {
      "asin": "B0COMP0003",
      "rating": 5,
      "ref": "R8",
      "text": "Still cold at the end of the school day."
    }
  ]
}
</input>

messages.content:
The input holds "items" to judge and the product "contexts" they refer to.
Each item has an "id", a "type", and either a "keyword" with a "context"
reference, or two "phrases". Judge every item on its own; items do not
influence each other.

type "relevance": how relevant the keyword is to the product in its context.
"score" (0 to 1):
- 0.9-1.0: names this exact product type and its defining attributes.
- 0.6-0.8: clearly the right product type, but generic or missing a key attribute.
- 0.3-0.5: related, but a different variant, audience, or feature this product
  is not shown to have.
- 0.0-0.2: a different product, a competitor's brand, or a non-shopping query.
Judge only from the product title and seed keywords. Treat any feature not
stated there as unknown.

type "intent": the search intent behind the keyword. "label" is one of:
- transactional: ready to buy a specific kind of item.
- commercial_investigation: comparing or browsing options.
- informational: wants information, not a product.
- navigational: looking for a specific brand, store, or listing.
"score" (0 to 1) is the strength of purchase intent: 1.0 for a precise
ready-to-buy query, around 0.5 for browsing, near 0 for informational queries.

type "entity": does the keyword name an entity the seller may not use in their
own listing or backend keywords? "label" is one of:
- none: generic words only.
- brand: a company or product brand.
- author: a person's name used as an author reference.
- trademark: a trademarked term or program name (for example a subscription
  program) that is not a brand of a physical product.
- product_line: a named product line or series of another company.
- other: some other proper name.
Put the entity text in "entity", or an empty string when the label is "none".
Words from the product title in the context belong to the seller, not to
another company.

type "equivalence": the two phrases use the same words in a different order.
"equivalent" is true only if a shopper typing either phrase wants the same kind
of product. Word order that changes the product (for example "bottle water", a
drink, versus "water bottle", a container) means they are not equivalent.

For every item set "confidence" (0 to 1) to how sure you are and give a
"rationale" of at most 25 words that a reviewer can check against the input.

Return exactly one result per item in "results", copying the item's "id" and
"type" exactly. Do not skip, merge, or add items. Result order does not matter.

<input>
{
  "contexts": {},
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "eqv-674b48f652",
      "phrases": [
        "bottle water",
        "water bottle"
      ],
      "type": "equivalence"
    },
    {
      "id": "eqv-03e4ab3683",
      "phrases": [
        "kids water bottle",
        "water bottles for kids"
      ],
      "type": "equivalence"
    }
  ]
}
</input>
